_comment: Per-clip ingest config for the SECOND clip — a distinct ~12s goal window of best-goals-2025-30s.mov (a different real goal than the single-goal hero, so the codegen `hint` genuinely differs). Carries the same HUMAN knowledge the hero manifest does: where the .mov lives, which window to sample, which detection is the scorer, the pinned jersey number (#7 here, NOT the hero's #10), and the goal moment. `source` resolves relative to this manifest dir. Sampling stride matches op_sample_frames (stride=round(1000/fps)); fps=8 -> stride 125, so 12000 (goal) and 12125 (pin/scorer frame) are both in the sampled list. This manifest drives the Alt-C derive of api/examples/best-goal_cache.json via FakeAzureVision(objects=fake_detect_best-goal.json) — no creds, deterministic.

pins._comment: Renames the detection nearest this box (at frame_ts_ms 12125) to the semantic id `p_seven` AND pins its jersey read to '7'. The match box is the scorer's person box (conf 0.712, x=0.105 in fake_detect_best-goal.json).

read_text.note: Hand-verified pin for the second clip's scorer (#7). Distinct from the hero's #10 so the new filter/read_text queries ground on a different value. (Alt-C deterministic derive — no live OCR.)

events._comment: The known goal moment for this clip. scorer_pin refers to the pin det_id (p_seven); the pipeline derives events[].scorer_det FROM the pin resolution, so the join key stays byte-identical across detect/read_text/events. A positive temporal claim, so the filter-#7 query grounds to Yes; the out-of-bounds filter-#99 query still grounds out honestly because it matches no det.

evidence_frames._comment: Stills the pipeline emits for completeness. NOTE: EvidencePanel.frameSrc hardcodes the hero's two stills (ts<=4200 -> goal-4000.jpg else scorer-4625.jpg) and does NOT read these filenames, so a new clip's stills won't render in the UI — generalizing that lookup is OUT of scope. Stills are emitted for completeness only.
